summary.text: Opens a 1982 French-language study of tetanus vaccination in rural African children, reporting that after one or two doses of adsorbed toxoid nearly all children reached protective antibody levels, with higher levels after two doses. It notes that moderate malnutrition and Plasmodium falciparum infection had no detectable short-term effect on antibody response, while unweaned children responded better after a single dose. The introduction explains why a shorter vaccination schedule matters where health infrastructure is weak, and the methods begin describing the children studied and the vaccine and dosing used.

sections.title: Programme

summary.text: Describes how children were classed as well nourished or malnourished by weight against reference norms and how malaria infection was assessed by blood smear, with intermediate-weight children excluded. It also outlines a preliminary check for pre-existing tetanus immunity in two groups of young children from an isolated village and a town with a dispensary.

summary.text: Details the blood sampling schedule, cold-chain transport of samples to a laboratory in Ouagadougou, and the separation of plasma for antibody testing. It then presents results on antibody levels after one or two injections, comparing groups by nutritional status, weaning and malaria infection. Figures show the distribution of antitetanus antibody titres among malaria-infected and uninfected children.

sections.title: bonne

summary.text: Discusses the reliability of the radioimmunoassay used and the limited survey of pre-vaccination immunity, which suggested more natural exposure in the isolated rural village but on too small a sample to conclude. It considers why malnutrition and malaria did not appear to impair the antibody response and the effect of breastfeeding. The authors conclude cautiously that malaria had no significant effect on antitetanus antibody responses in children aged 1 to 3 years and that any effect of antimalarial drugs cannot be determined.

sections.title: ANTITETANUS ANTIBODY RESPONSES

summary.text: The English summary of the antibody findings, reporting that nearly all of 414 children aged 1-3 years reached measurable antitetanus antibody levels after one or two toxoid doses, with two doses giving higher levels. It adds that nutritional status and malaria infection made no difference, while breastfed children responded better after one dose only.

sections.extract: Serum antibody levels were determined by specific radio- immunoassay in 414 children aged 1- 3 years, 7- 8 weeks after one or two injections of adsorbed tetanus toxoid (124 IU/ml). Studies in a small group of non-immunized children showed that the possibility of preimmunization antibodies being present in some individuals could be neglected in interpreting postimmunization data.
